newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai, S&P officials to meet next week.
newsitem.headline: Thai, S&P officials to meet next week.

text.p: Officials of credit rating agency Standard & Poor's Corp are scheduled to meet with Thai government officials next week after issuing a negative creditwatch on Thailand, a finance ministry official said on Friday.
The official said S&P officials would hold talks with authorities from the finance ministry, central bank and the National Economic and Social Development Board in Bangkok.
S&P officials will also gather information on the Thai economy during their stay to use in their reports.
S&P said on Friday it had placed a negative creditwatch on Thai foreign currency and eight financial institutions, including the country's largest bank, Bangkok Bank Plc.
The ratings agency said its action reflected concerns that non-performing loans and loan losses would rise to levels not consistent with current ratings.

Thailand is also having talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and finance minister Thanong Bidaya is due to present a series of measures next Tuesday which are aimed at boosting the sagging economy.

These are expected to be in line with IMF recommendations on tough measures Thailand needs to take to improve its economic situation. It is not clear if it will include the announcement of any IMF loans or standby credit lines.
